rows.note: Fluidity SLO: 99% of requests with <10% deadline miss rate at 25 ms target TBT; TPOT and P99-TBT baselines use target latency of 25 ms. Etalon finds max QPS meeting the SLO.
Fluidity-index capacity printed in text as same for both systems at 0.6 QPS.
Printed in text: same at 0.6 QPS (bar read ~0.62).
Visible panel is ArxivSumm (y axis 0-1.2 QPS/s). Linear axis, gridlines 0.2; read against gridlines.
As above. Text: Sarathi has 2x lower token throughput than vLLM by tail-TBT metric (0.65/0.35 ~1.9).

Printed: 'Sarathi has a 2x lower token throughput compared to vLLM as measured by tail TBT-based metric, in contrast to Figure 3.' Almost all mixed batches with prefill chunks violate the 25 ms threshold.

Deadline of token i: D_i = D_p + i*D_d. D_p = target prefill latency as function of prompt length (profiling vLLM in isolation, 10 requests tunable, curve fit); Alg.1 line 2: D_p = predict_prefill_time(P) + SD (scheduling slack SD). Early tokens bank slack (slack += D - t); on a miss, misses = floor((t - slack - D)/D_d)+1, slack reset to 0 and later deadlines reset. fluidity-index = (total - missed)/total deadlines.
Fluid token generation rate = inverse of the minimum D_d such that 99% of requests have fluidity-index >= 0.9 (Fig. 3 caption writes '> 0.9').
Worked example: target TBT 100 ms; system with 10 tokens at 10 ms and 11th at 150 ms has the same TBT miss rate as one with 10 tokens at 100 ms and 11th at 150 ms.
